Paper betsDoes betting on the model pay?

Every bet is placed by a fixed rule, nothing hand-picked. Since Oct 25 only game-line rules run, priced from nflverse's free line feed at the last morning update before kickoff; rules that needed DraftKings prop prices stopped (their graded bets stay below). Flat 1 unit each; a player who doesn't play is a push. Expected is how many the model said would hit. Main tests were picked on Oct 22, before any had results, and each has a fixed number of bets it needs (shown as "Too early (12 of 100)"); it earns trust with a profit and a hit rate clearly above break-even (2 standard errors). Every other rule is exploratory: with this many rules running, some will look good by luck, so they need 150+ bets and a much stronger result (3 standard errors). Same-game stacks and ML + top TD scorer have no real price, so they're graded on whether the model's chance was right. Open a group for its rules or bets.

CombosWhen the model says these all happen, do they?

No odds involved. Before each game, fixed rules pair the model's predictions into 2- and 3-part combos at round, bettable thresholds (50+ rush yds, 4+ catches, 225+ pass yds), each leg picked where the model gives it about a 70% chance. A combo's chance accounts for how its parts move together in the same game (a QB's big day lifts his top receiver). A combo with a scratched player is set aside. The random pairs are the control. Exploratory: a type means little before about 150 graded combos.
